oewn-00749644-v.learner: to start speaking, or to start saying something.
examples: As soon as they entered the copse, Lady Catherine began in the following manner
Mrs. Bennet and Kitty walked off, and as soon as they were gone, Mr. Collins began

oewn-00346415-v.learner: to take the first step or steps in carrying something out.
examples: unable to contain herself, began scolding one of her daughters
He began writing the letter as soon as he sat down.

oewn-02615238-v.learner: for an event in time to have its start.
examples: The ball began at eight o'clock and lasted until morning.

oewn-05954491-n.learner: a belief or judgement of your own that rests on no proof and is not certain.
examples: "Upon my word," said Mrs. Gardiner, "I begin to be of your uncle's opinion.
Can there be any other opinion on the subject?

oewn-06794876-n.learner: words that say what you believe; you hold the belief firmly, but you cannot prove it or know it for sure.
examples: She gave her opinion of the plan aloud, so that everyone in the room heard it.

oewn-05925333-n.learner: an idea that is not clear or exact, but that you trust to some degree.
examples: to adopt any opinions that came in her way

oewn-08647614-n.learner: the stretch of space where something is; an area of a larger place.
examples: I was fortunate enough to find out in what part of London they were
Mr. Darcy would no more suffer him to call on Jane in such a part of London!

oewn-13831419-n.learner: a thing seen in terms of the bigger thing that takes it in.
examples: he had all the best parts of beauty, a fine countenance, a good figure, and very pleasing address

oewn-05679818-n.learner: what concerns one person, given the role or the situation that person is in.
examples: On the other hand, I, for my part, declare for Pride and Prejudice unhesitatingly.

oewn-09408804-n.learner: a piece of a thing that occurs in nature.
examples: which brought them again, after some time, in a descent among hanging woods, to the edge of the water, and one of its narrowest parts

oewn-00099264-r.learner: instead of that; the opposite is what is so.
examples: I am much mistaken if there are not some among us to whom a ball would be rather a punishment than a pleasure.
The separation between her and her family was rather noisy than pathetic.

oewn-00018764-r.learner: to some degree, whether a large one or a small one.
examples: that this adventure has rather affected your admiration of her fine eyes

oewn-13984685-n.learner: the way one person's existence runs, with the things they do and the things that happen while they live.
examples: The business of her life was to get her daughters married: its solace was visiting and news.
teaching her that her present pursuits are not to be the business of her life

oewn-13984978-n.learner: the condition of living; the state of being alive.
examples: considering what her anxiety for his life had been before

oewn-15165365-n.learner: the length of time during which something works or lives, as from birth to death.

oewn-05619057-n.learner: the part of a person that holds thoughts and feelings and keeps you aware, and where reasoning is done.
examples: Her mind was less difficult to develope.
her mind opened again to the agitation of hope

oewn-05846466-n.learner: a view you reach after weighing something up.
examples: He would not change his mind about the invitation.

oewn-05770146-n.learner: the bringing of something back to memory.

oewn-02002464-v.learner: to move along behind someone or something, going after them.

oewn-02726229-v.learner: to come after something in time, as a result of it.

oewn-02718647-v.learner: to come at a later time than something else.

oewn-01735600-a.learner: of the time that is now, between the past and the future: existing, happening, or being considered at this time.

oewn-01852337-a.learner: being there in a stated place.

oewn-01230397-n.learner: the act of showing that you have regard for other people.

oewn-00555499-s.learner: ready to agree to something, or to give consent to it.
